findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47 — UsernameForm.authenticate() calls the no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` but the only method defined (in UsernamePasswordForm.java:160) is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, so this file does not compile, meaning the entire re-authentication passkey fix (and any test suite validating it) cannot even build.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:115 — isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) only checks that a user is set and passkeys are enabled realm-wide — it does not check whether that specific user actually has any registered passkey credential — so fillContextForm/webauthn UI is unconditionally injected into the re-authentication password form for every user, relying entirely on downstream shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()==false in the conditional authenticator to avoid an authenticator-list lookup; any future change to that override (or another Authenticator subclass being wired in as webauthnAuth) could silently reintroduce the empty-authenticator-list early return (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:104-107) and break the reauth form entirely for passkey-less users.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47 — UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments but the only method defined (in parent UsernamePasswordForm) is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), so this does not resolve to the same API and appears to reference a missing/mismatched overload, breaking the new SPI extension point contract.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:115 — challenge()/authenticate() webauthn setup condition changed from requiring context.getUser() == null to requiring context.getUser() != null (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled inverts the null-check), silently reversing behavior that third-party subclasses overriding these protected methods may depend on.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:137 — challenge() now shows webauthn form when a user IS already set (previously only when no user selected), a behavioral inversion of a protected method third-party Authenticator SPI implementations may override or call via super.challenge().

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 — New protected method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) is added as an extension point but its semantics (webauthn enabled AND user non-null) are non-obvious and undocumented for subclasses relying on the previous inline conditions.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:101 — New protected method shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) replaces the previous inline "user != null" check in challenge(); third-party subclasses that already override challenge() and duplicate the old inline logic will not pick up new conditional-passkey behavior, and any existing subclass with a method of the same signature/name could silently change behavior.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:136 — WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides the new shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) to unconditionally return false, changing behavior inherited from WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator/WebAuthnAuthenticator for any third-party subclass of this class that expected the base class's user-presence check.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47 — UsernameForm.authenticate() calls the no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` but the only method defined (in UsernamePasswordForm.java:160) is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, so this file does not compile, meaning the entire re-authentication passkey fix (and any test suite validating it) cannot even build.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:115 — isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) only checks that a user is set and passkeys are enabled realm-wide — it does not check whether that specific user actually has any registered passkey credential — so fillContextForm/webauthn UI is unconditionally injected into the re-authentication password form for every user, relying entirely on downstream shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()==false in the conditional authenticator to avoid an authenticator-list lookup; any future change to that override (or another Authenticator subclass being wired in as webauthnAuth) could silently reintroduce the empty-authenticator-list early return (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:104-107) and break the reauth form entirely for passkey-less users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernamePasswordForm` to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true (i.e., `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`), without checking whether the identified user has any WebAuthn/passkey credentials. At the same time, `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` now gates the authenticator-list lookup behind `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)`, and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides that to always return `false`, implicitly relying on that override to avoid the empty-authenticator-list early-return path. This is a diff-grounded robustness/maintenance concern (tight coupling + no per-user credential check), but the diff does not demonstrate an actual broken behavior today.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:137 — challenge() now shows webauthn form when a user IS already set (previously only when no user selected), a behavioral inversion of a protected method third-party Authenticator SPI implementations may override or call via super.challenge().

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a clear behavioral inversion in `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext, String, String)`: it changed from `if (context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }` to `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }`, where `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` requires `user != null`. So the webauthn context setup in `challenge()` now happens only when a user is already set, whereas previously it happened only when no user was selected. This appears intentional given the accompanying tests and related changes, but it is still a notable SPI/extension-compatibility concern because subclasses calling `super.challenge()` will now get different behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 — New protected method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) is added as an extension point but its semantics (webauthn enabled AND user non-null) are non-obvious and undocumented for subclasses relying on the previous inline conditions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in `UsernamePasswordForm` and replaces prior inline conditionals with this helper (e.g., in `authenticate()` and `challenge()`). The helper’s semantics include a non-obvious `user != null` requirement (`return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;`) and it has no Javadoc/comments explaining why “conditional passkeys” depends on having a user. Since it’s `protected` (and therefore plausibly intended to be overridden/relied upon by subclasses), the lack of documentation and the potentially misleading name is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/extension-point concern, not a directly verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:101 — New protected method shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) replaces the previous inline "user != null" check in challenge(); third-party subclasses that already override challenge() and duplicate the old inline logic will not pick up new conditional-passkey behavior, and any existing subclass with a method of the same signature/name could silently change behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the inline `user != null` check is replaced inside `fillContextForm()` (not in `challenge()`). The new `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` method currently just returns `context.getUser() != null`, so no new “conditional-passkey behavior” is introduced here to be missed by subclasses overriding `challenge()`. While adding a new protected hook could theoretically interact with third-party subclasses, the finding’s concrete claims about `challenge()` and conditional-passkeys are not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:136 — WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides the new shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) to unconditionally return false, changing behavior inherited from WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator/WebAuthnAuthenticator for any third-party subclass of this class that expected the base class's user-presence check.

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally introduces a hook method `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` in `WebAuthnAuthenticator` (defaulting to `context.getUser() != null`) and then overrides it in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` to return `false` with an explicit comment: "Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys". This is a deliberate behavior customization for the conditional UI authenticator, not a verifiable defect. The finding’s claim about breaking “any third-party subclass ... that expected the base class's user-presence check” is speculative and not something that can be verified from the PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58 — USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth-note constant visibility widened from protected to public, exposing an internal auth-session note key as public API that third-party code may now read/write directly, coupling external code to an internal implementation detail.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` from `protected static final` to `public static final` (line ~58). This widens visibility to allow access from `AuthenticatorUtils` (which now `static import`s it from a different package), but it also exposes an internal auth-session note key as a public constant that external/third-party code could start depending on or manipulating, increasing coupling to an internal implementation detail. This is a scope/API design concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/util/AuthenticatorUtils.java:168 — New public static helper setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(AuthenticationFlowContext) duplicates/replaces logic previously inline in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, becoming a new public surface that custom authenticators may now call but whose exact form-attribute side effects are undocumented.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the re-authentication error-form setup logic was moved from inline code in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler` into a new `public static` method `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(AuthenticationFlowContext)` (and is now also called from `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator`). This does expand the public utility surface and centralizes side-effectful behavior (setting `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` based on the auth note). While there is a brief comment, there is no stronger API contract/Javadoc documenting the exact form-attribute side effects, so the review concern is grounded but architectural rather than a demonstrable defect.
